heroHeadline: Day 24: MSF Documents Mass Atrocities Among 300,000 Malian Refugees in Mauritania; Kidal Airstrikes Continue; Bamako Siege Holds
heroSubtitle: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) disclosed on May 19–21 that its staff in Doueinkara, eastern Mauritania, are documenting systematic torture, sexual violence against women and men, beheadings, being burned alive, and massacres among the ~300,000 Malian refugees sheltering in Mauritania's Hodh Chargui region — MSF coordinator Mayoury Savant described testimonies depicting 'a level of horror rarely seen on such a scale in the region.' AFP photojournalists documented refugee accounts of FAMa and Africa Corps atrocities in northern Mali. The MSF disclosures coincide with the African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights case filed April 20 by FIDH, TRIAL International, and the Pan African Lawyers Union — the first-ever case against a state for hosting and contracting private military actors. On the military front, FAMa and Africa Corps continue their aerial campaign against FLA/JNIM-held Kidal with Su-type fighters and armed drones (10+ airstrikes in recent days per Pravda Mali); a joint reconnaissance near the Nion settlement (Ségou Region) on May 20 discovered and neutralized a militant observer; and FAMa air strikes hit a terrorist base in the Dyafarabe area. However, Kidal remains under FLA control, the Bamako supply blockade holds on Day 24 (3 of 6 corridors disrupted, food prices +43–65%, IRC emergency response active, WFP suspended), and JNIM's IED campaign against FAMa patrol routes in Mopti Region continues. JNIM-aligned Ansaroul Islam's evacuation warning for Djibo signals an imminent second major assault on the besieged Burkinabe provincial capital, while the AES Unified Force's 15,000 authorized strength has not arrested the multi-country simultaneous strike tempo that has defined the crisis since April 25.
